To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the transferability of experimental findings to a new target population is feasible if and only if the target population is a mixture of the experimental and the observational populations, and (b) the transfer formula is a mixture of two estimators: one that estimates the causal effect in the experimental population, and the second one that estimates the mixing proportion.

transportability can be decided by the presence or absence of the following four conditions:
  1. (a) A set of assumptions concerning the differences between the target population and the source population.

transportability of experimental results is feasible if and only if the following two conditions hold: (a) the causal effect is invariant with respect to the target population, and (b) the causal effect can be estimated from the observational data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of transferring information learned in experiments to other populations, where only observational studies are available.
the problem of transferring information across populations.
the problem of how to combine information from experiments with information from observational studies to estimate the causal effects of interventions in a target population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

transportability is feasible when the following two conditions are met: (1) there exists a causal graph that satisfies the assumptions of the target population; and (2) the experimental data are sufficient for computing the causal effect in the target population.
transportability of experimental results is possible only if the target population is a special case of the experimental population.

transportability is feasible if, and only if, there exists an observational study in which all the confounders are measured and the experimental study is conducted in a manner that satisfies the conditions of transportability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
transportability is a special case of generalizability that can be solved by a general algorithm.

transportability is a special case of the general problem of causal discovery from multiple sources, and that the algorithm presented in this paper can be applied to any causal discovery problem, not only transportability.

we present a general framework for deciding whether experimental results are transportable to new settings, and, when they are, how to synthesize the information from experiments and observations to obtain a transport formula.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transfer of information between experiments and observational studies is not a one-way street.

transportability can be decided algorithmically, and that the transport formula can be computed effectively, thus making it possible to transfer experimental information to observational studies in a principled manner.
transportability is a well-defined and practical problem, which can be solved by the proposed algorithm.
